name: Strait of Hormuz
description: Strategic chokepoint between Persian Gulf and Gulf of Oman. ~20% of global oil transit. Critical for Iraq, Saudi Arabia, UAE, Kuwait, Qatar exports to India.
notes: ~42% of India's crude imports transit Hormuz (Iraq+Saudi+UAE+Kuwait)

name: Red Sea / Bab el-Mandeb
description: Connects Gulf of Aden to Suez Canal. Houthi attacks since 2023 have disrupted shipping. Affects Mediterranean-routed crude to India.
notes: Limited direct India crude dependency but affects Suez-routed shipments

name: Suez Canal
description: Connects Red Sea to Mediterranean. Critical for European crude flows. Some India-bound crude from Mediterranean sources.
notes: Minimal direct India crude dependency; affects alternate routing

name: Strait of Malacca
description: Connects Indian Ocean to South China Sea. Critical for East Asian energy supply. Less critical for India crude imports.
notes: Very low India crude dependency; mainly affects Southeast Asian routing

name: Russia Supplier Corridor
description: Russia as a supplier corridor. Crude exported from Baltic (Primorsk/Ust-Luga) and Pacific (Kozmino/ESPO). Subject to Western sanctions/price cap since 2022.
notes: ~36-38% of India's crude imports from Russia FY2025. Shadow fleet and sanctions risk.

name: Cape of Good Hope
description: Alternate routing around Africa. Used when Hormuz/Red Sea/Suez are disrupted. Significantly longer transit (~3x Hormuz route).
notes: Not a chokepoint but an alternate route. Low base risk. Freight multiplier ~3.2x vs Hormuz.
